top_choice_rationale: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson by two independent detectors is the largest unrecognised experimental result on the shortlist; its properties have been stable for over a decade and the 2013 prize covered only the theory. P002 (Gianotti, Jenni, Virdee) credits conception, construction and leadership across both experiments, with the CMS seat decided by the construction-through-first-data principle. P003 differs only in naming Della Negra instead of Virdee, a defensible but less preferred judgement, so it ranks second. The optical lattice clock (P001) is mature and has the cleanest two-name credit, but it overlaps with the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes and is the narrower result, so I rank it third, above no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; only general professional ties (two years at CERN, theoretical-physics field) with no documented connection to any proposed laureate
